liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Home of the Red Fox** (1 review): The opening instrumental, before the jam into How Mountain Girls, is Home of the Red Fox, written by Bill Emerson [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Takin' a Slow Train**: back after 66 archived shows (371 days); rare: 10 archived performances [8]
- **Home of the Red Fox > How Mountain Girls Can Love**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]
- **Idumea**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [8]
- **To Lay Me Down**: rare: 13 archived performances [8]
- **I'm Gone, Long Gone**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 10 archived performances [8]

## The recordings

- **billystrings2018-07-20.fm.flac16** (recommended): FM broadcast; 10 songs; 74 min [1]
- **BillyStrings2018-07-20.HighMeadow.4041.flac16**: source not stated; 10 songs; 72 min; rated 4/5 by 5 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer skipped this set for Red Knuckles; Methro couldn't appear because of his own main stage set [4]
- Mentions a separate festival Doc Watson tribute set with Bryan Sutton, Billy Strings and Joe Newbury, a highlight for the reviewer [4]
- Commenter notes bluelawn taped many Grey Fox sets, including Billy Strings and Sierra Hull sets awaiting etree upload [7]

## Tapers and lineage

- **billystrings2018-07-20.fm.flac16**: source: FM receiver > PC > CDWAV > edited in CDWAV > FLAC 1 [1]
- **BillyStrings2018-07-20.HighMeadow.4041.flac16**: taped by Seth Nochajski & Keith Januszak; transferred by Seth Nochajski; source: Audio-Technica 4041s > NADY Audio DMP-2 > Tascam DR-05 [24/48] [2]. Also: The Sierra / Billy set will eventually go on bt.etree.org; the commenter did not tape the Sierra / Sam workshop; Transferred from MicroSD to PC, edited in Sound Forge Pro 11, dithered and resampled to 44.1 kHz, then converted to 16-bit FLAC [2][6]
